Don't confuse true religion for the politics of the symbol,
Nor allow yourself to be taken by the new religion of symbolic politics.
Politics is family dynamics,
Religion too.
Politics the family of the many and the few,
Religion the family of zero and one, the family where zero and one make one and two…
Our political family becomes religion
When god goes the way of the homing pigeon,
And sets for the nest after a long excursion.
Our religious family becomes politics
When faiths become mere stones and sticks,
And God is made
Fixed fast for Psyche's di-version.
Stones and sticks are not just arms
They are idols and crutches, both
Receivers of feeble clutches,
Ready for when the quiet harms
The delicacies of our existential suspension
Within God's devotion and law, the charms of Being,
Which, like the solace of seeing,
Is truest when
It goes without mention.
That which lobbies without lexicon is truly free of pretension.
Is it not truth and freedom that ought breathe through politics and religion alike?
Ambrosial joys for which we ought have more than a mere penchant
But a sublime yearning, trenchant, for which alone is earning
The dignity to rise and realise the family of the light
Burning atop the cresting night
As Earth dreams again of the divine,
Having, it seems, outstripped earthly delight.
